messages:
sara: Heads-up — bringing up mistral-7b-v2 on the canary pool. With kv_prefetch enabled we see p95 spike and occasional mem churn. Anyone seen similar with prefetch on long-context workloads?

yun: saw this pattern on a different model last month. kv_prefetch can cause more frequent KV cache allocations and evictions which fragments GPU memory over time.

sara: yeah, interesting. On canary: p50 ~120ms, p95 jumped 360ms (was ~210ms on baseline), and one node hit an OOM after ~4h of steady traffic.

kevin: can you share the route config? also what's max_new_tokens you're using for the tests?

sara: route config below (canary):

```yaml
model: mistral-7b-v2
max_new_tokens: 512
max_batch_size: 16
max_batch_tokens: 8192
kv_prefetch: true
kv_cache_eviction: lru
batching_window_ms: 40
```

sara: test workload is long-context summarization, median input ~4k tokens.

yun: 16 max_batch_size + high max_batch_tokens + kv_prefetch on long contexts = big KV working set in memory. When the runtime does continuous batching it increases resident set and evictions. Fragmentation follows.

david: saw OOMs too on dedicated nodes when batch_size spiked. On one host the allocator never returned freed pages back to the OS quickly enough. We're rolling a jemalloc tweak to reduce retention; will try on canary.

kevin: quick experiments I’d run: 1) disable kv_prefetch (or set to adaptive), 2) reduce max_batch_size to 4–8, 3) cap max_batch_tokens lower for long-context routes, 4) try max_new_tokens 256 as default for this route.

sara: doing a quick toggle: disabling kv_prefetch and set max_batch_size=6, max_new_tokens=256, batching_window_ms=20. Pushing canary now.

deploy-bot: deploy started -> canary: mistral-7b-v2 @ canary-pool-3 by sara (1769851205)

eval-bot: running perf probes on canary (seq=1..50)

sara: results after toggles (approx): p50 130ms, p95 240ms, no OOMs in 2h. memory RSS growth much flatter. :thumbsup:

kevin: nice. That suggests kv_prefetch was the main contributor. We should add a route-level heuristic: disable prefetch if median input length > 2k or if max_batch_tokens > 6k.

yun: agree. Also consider making kv_prefetch adaptive: only prefetch when current request fits entirely in a per-request budget, otherwise stream and reuse KV pages.

david: patch for jemalloc background tuning landed in canary branch; it helps fragmentation but doesn't solve the root cause here. I'll keep it in the rollout.

sara: can we standardize a safer default for new model bring-ups? Proposed defaults for model onboarding doc: max_new_tokens=256, max_batch_size=8, max_batch_tokens=4096, kv_prefetch=false (enable behind opt-in for long short-context routes), batching_window_ms=20.

kevin: +1. Also add a short checklist: run 4h steady-state traffic, check RSS delta, p95, and verify no OOMs on at least 3 hosts.

yun: will add an automated eval that sweeps kv_prefetch true/false and records fragmentation metrics (alloc/free patterns). Helpful to capture small traces of allocator behavior.

deploy-bot: canary health check passed -> promoting to small rollout (1769851490)

sara: thanks all. Follow-ups: yun + kevin to add adaptive prefetch RFC; david to monitor allocator metrics post-rollout; i'll update onboarding doc and default route template.

kev: one last note — if teams need high max_new_tokens (>=512) for gen-heavy apps, recommend isolated dedicated pools with larger GPU and dedicated eviction policy instead of enabling prefetch on shared pools.

sara: noted. closing thread when docs PR is up.
